note: Single-screen clear-all-enemies arcade; the deliberate non-scrolling test case for the discovery pipeline. All observables below come from this session's own rollouts (headless Pool, our verified ram_mapping); no external RAM maps or disassembly.

step1_start_state_capture.result: gameplay confirmed at frame 1695 (+40 settle frames), wrote 45745 bytes
step1_start_state_capture.verification: is_controllable() growth+directionality gate (RIGHT vs LEFT vs base RAM diff) passed automatically inside the capture tool

step2_discovery.method: scripts/discover_observables.py (automated wrap+saturation gates) + a dedicated 12,000-step heuristic-random probe (frame_skip 4, full 2KB scan) + a dedicated jump-in-place probe, all from the captured start state

rejected_spatial_candidate.wrap_test: PASSED naively: rises under a forward RIGHT hold, flat under NOOP
rejected_spatial_candidate.saturation_test: FAILED (rejected): under a sustained 500-step RIGHT hold rises 26->224 then sits DEAD FLAT for the remainder of the probe while the character keeps animating (not frozen) -- classic camera-clamp/screen-edge signature; under a sustained LEFT hold rises to only 17 and stays flat. No page/room byte pairs with it (find_page/find_room_counter both returned none) -- there is nothing beyond this one fixed screen to pair with, confirming the game genuinely has no world-X frontier.
rejected_spatial_candidate.conclusion: screen-bound pixel coordinate, not world position. discover_observables.py's automated pass independently reached the same verdict: '[recommended progress] none' from the naive zero-page scan (all zero-page candidates were free-running counters that also moved heavily under NOOP, correctly rejected by gate 1).

evidence: flat for hundreds/thousands of steps within a round (only 3 total transitions across the whole 12,000-step probe)

both transitions corroborated by a full-scene-reload RAM signature: 194 and 533 (of 2048) bytes changed in that single step -- enemy/OAM object arrays reset, player respawns at the canonical Y=80 start pose (matches frame-0 OAM Y=80)
both transitions corroborated by the enemies-remaining counter (0x0496, see boss: below) reading exactly 0 immediately beforehand
lives (0x002E) UNCHANGED at both transitions (2, then 1) -- proves these are real round clears, not a death/reset artifact aliasing the same byte
independent of lives: 3 separate real deaths occurred in the same probe (steps 127, 876, 2947, lives 3->2->1->0) with 0x0401 NOT moving at any of them

lives_signal.manual_confirmation: 3 clean decrements (3->2->1->0) across the 12k-step probe at steps 127, 876, 2947, each coincident with an OAM position reset (respawn) and independent of the round counter

step2_discovery.death_signal: is_dead fires on lives-decrement (lives < start_lives); no separate clean player_state/death byte was pursued given the lives signal is already unambiguous

resets to a fresh count after every round transition: round 1 starts at 3, rounds 2 and 3 both start at 4
reads exactly 0 immediately before both observed round-clear transitions (step 627 -> 0, held until the step-756 clear; step 1553 -> 0, held until the step-1682 clear)
bonus_find_enemy_count.not_required_by_schema: GenericGame's required fields (progress/y/level_key/lives) don't need this; included as an optional solve.boss hook because this non-scrolling game otherwise has NO in-round exploration axis besides y-band

step2_discovery.full_2kb_scan: performed (not zero-page-only): custom probe scanned all 0x800 bytes under clean RIGHT/LEFT/NOOP holds and the 12,000-step heuristic-random play log; the only flat-under-NOOP/rises-under-forward candidates in the full scan were 0x0203/0x0207 (OAM X, rejected above) -- no other spatial byte was found anywhere in RAM, consistent with a genuinely non-scrolling game

step3_solve_config_written.level_key_note: NOT the usual coverage-baseline empty list. Unlike Contra/Kirby/DuckTales (all ship level_key: [] because no receipted stage-advance byte exists), Bubble Bobble's round counter doubles as a clean, receipted clear signal -- 'increments each cleared single screen' literally IS is_clear here (see step2 evidence).

checks.rollout: 300 steps x 3 workers, mixed RIGHT+B / LEFT+B / A+B actions

step5_solve_run.wall_clock: 360s (6 minutes, hit the time budget; want_solutions=4 was not reached)
step5_solve_run.throughput: 382,851 total env steps across 3 workers, ~1069 steps/s aggregate
step5_solve_run.cell_saturation_note: all 32 reachable cells were found within the first ~60s (new_cells stayed at 32 for the remaining 5 minutes) -- the non-spatial cell key (area constant 0, progress-bucket constant 0 while round<16, so diversity reduces to hp(0-4) x sig(0) x y-band) has very low resolution for this game, exactly the stress-test the task called for
step5_solve_run.max_progress_reached: round 2 (level_key advance 1->2), all 3 solutions; round 3 was never reached within this 6-minute solve
step5_solve_run.trajectory_refinement: 297 -> 232 -> 217 actions (27% shorter) purely through the archive revisiting/improving cells -- a capability blind random cannot replicate

step5b_random_baseline_comparison.purpose: the actual OUT-TRAVELS-RANDOM validation requested by the task
step5b_random_baseline_comparison.method: uniform-random policy over the SAME profile action_space, SAME GenericGame adapter, SAME 3 workers, matched to the identical 360s (6-minute) wall-clock budget; on death OR a 4000-step life cap, the worker reloads the captured start state (memoryless restart -- no archive, no return mechanism, the textbook Go-Explore-vs-random comparator)
step5b_random_baseline_comparison.honest_verdict: Go-Explore did NOT out-travel random on raw round-depth in this run: one random worker reached round 3 once, while all 3 Go-Explore solutions capped at round 2. Two receipted reasons: (1) round 1 is intrinsically easy -- ANY reasonably active policy clears it (blind random's first clear appeared after only 2,985 aggregate env steps, and it clocked 57 total clears vs Go-Explore's 3 in the identical 6-minute budget); (2) the impoverished non-spatial cell key saturates the archive almost immediately (all 32 cells found in ~60s), so Go-Explore's remaining ~300K steps had no fresh frontier to push into and were spent re-sampling the same 32 cells rather than reaching deeper rounds.
step5b_random_baseline_comparison.where_go_explore_did_show_real_value: trajectory quality, not reachability. Its best verified solution (217 actions) is 17% shorter than random's best out of 57 tries (262 actions) and 66% shorter than random's median (636 actions), produced via principled iterative refinement (297->232->217) that a memoryless random-restart process cannot do by construction -- it has no mechanism to improve on a lucky success.
step5b_random_baseline_comparison.pipeline_lesson: for a single-screen, no-scroll game the standard (area, hp, sig, y-band, progress-bucket) cell key is too coarse to give the archive a meaningful frontier once the one and only per-round objective (the round clear) is reachable by luck alone; a real depth advantage for Go-Explore here would need either a finer in-round cell signal (e.g. enemy-slot state combinatorics beyond a single hp scalar) or the same level-chaining used for scrolling games (re-root a fresh solve at a harvested round-2 arrival state to push into round 3), which is out of scope for this single bootstrap run.

step6_observatory_v2.archive_size_caveat: only 32 cells existed to sample (see cell-saturation note above), so pass-1 probed all 32 and pass-2 targeted 2 more (34 total, 24-step probes) -- support counts (10-22 out of ~34) are on the small side; treat ranks as suggestive, not conclusive
